lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs have begun October by misplacing their margin for error. Saturday's 3-2 loss to Ottawa left Toronto 1-2-0, sixth in the Atlantic with two points and a one-game skid - hardly a crisis, but no foundation for complacency, either. Kirill Marchenko remains the encouraging exception: one goal and two points through three games, 19 shots on goal, and the kind of aggressive release that explains why Toronto paid heavily to get him. Gavin McKenna, meanwhile, is still searching for his first NHL point, and the line's rough opening has drawn scrutiny; patience is sensible, provided it does not become an excuse for drift. The injury list includes Max Domi, Dakota Joshua and Elvis Merzlikins, thinning the margins further. Tonight's 7 p.m. meeting with Nashville is the first chance to steady the ship - and to see whether Marchenko and Auston Matthews can pull McKenna into the current.

the_latest.headline: Senators benefited from later season opener against Leafs
the_latest.dek: Ottawa's delayed opener gave the Senators extra preparation time while Toronto entered the matchup already navigating a compressed start. The 3-2 loss leaves the Leafs at 1-2-0 and sixth in the Atlantic, adding urgency to tonight's home game against Nashville.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and the Blue Jays' 79-83 finish leaves no room for cosmetic repairs. The immediate development is the roster retool now taking shape, with second base the clearest test of whether Toronto trusts internal answers or goes shopping. Andrés Giménez is expected to hold shortstop, while Davis Schneider's path at second remains open - general manager Ross Atkins has made clear that earning the job matters. That is a decision, not a depth chart. The club finished fifth in the AL East, and its next version needs more than optimism: an impact bat, rotation depth and a firmer plan for a lineup that too often asked Vladimir Guerrero Jr. to carry the thunder. The Arizona Fall League offers a useful scouting window, while the Canadian Futures Showcase supplies a reminder that the pipeline needs ceiling, not merely bodies. Watch the second-base market, the pitching board and the organization's next move toward 2027.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors are learning that preseason is less about polishing a finished product than discovering which pieces can survive contact with October. Kawhi Leonard's first full practice since rejoining the team is the headline, but Toronto is wisely handling the star like fine china; he remains in reconditioning and is expected to sit Saturday against the Clippers. That caution matters after the Heat dismantled Toronto 129-105 on Oct. 3, an exhibition loss that counts nowhere but exposes plenty. Jakob Poeltl's offseason work on his back is another subplot, because Toronto's projected interior anchor cannot afford to limp into the season. The roster churn has begun, too: Tyson Degenhart is in, Andre Jackson Jr. is out. Watch the Clippers game Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET for lineup clues, then the Oct. 21 opener against Chicago for the real verdict.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The London trip turned into a quarterly report on Washington's fragility. The Commanders fell 30-13 to Indianapolis on Sunday, and the defeat exposed more than a bad afternoon: at 1-3, they sit fourth in the NFC East, two games behind, riding a one-game losing streak. Marcus Mariota's MCL injury made matters worse after he replaced the injured Jayden Daniels, forcing rookie Athan Kaliakmanis into the game. Now the season's hinge arrives in a familiar place - the quarterback room. Dan Quinn expects Daniels to practice fully this week after his dislocated left elbow, with the aim of returning Sunday. That is not a luxury; it is Washington's only credible route back into the fight. Watch whether Daniels can complete the week and start against the Giants at 1 p.m. ET Sunday on Fox - because another quarterback shuffle could turn a rough start into a lost season.

article.title: Commanders Expect Daniels to Start Sunday
paragraphs: The Washington Commanders expect Jayden Daniels to return to practice this week and start Sunday against the Giants, a welcome development after his elbow injury. Washington is 1-3 and sits fourth in the NFC East; kickoff is 1:00 PM ET on Fox.

The Leafs host Nashville at 7:00 PM on TSN, with Sergei Bobrovsky slated to face Juuse Annunen. Toronto is 1-2-0, and the early focus remains on patience with the McKenna line and a bigger contribution from Kirill Marchenko. The Blue Jays are turning toward a 2027 roster retool, with second base among the positions to address.
The Raptors have Kawhi Leonard back in full practice as they prepare for Saturday's preseason game against the Clippers. Their regular season opens October 21 against the Bulls at 7:30 PM ET.
